title: Geometry - Lesson 3 Practice: Triangle Similarity by AA
description: Practice identifying AA similarity from angle marks, parallel-line evidence, and vertex correspondence.

questions.question: Which evidence is enough to prove two triangles are similar by AA?
options: Two pairs of equal side lengths only
questions.explanation: AA similarity requires two pairs of congruent corresponding angles.

questions.question: If $\angle A \cong \angle D$ and $\angle B \cong \angle E$, which similarity statement has the correct order?
questions.explanation: $A$ matches $D$ and $B$ matches $E$, so the remaining vertices match as $C \leftrightarrow F$.

questions.question: One pair of congruent angles is enough to prove two triangles are similar by AA.
questions.explanation: AA similarity needs two pairs of congruent angles, not just one.

questions.question: Complete the reason: If two pairs of corresponding angles in two triangles are congruent, then the triangles are similar by ______ similarity.
questions.explanation: The shortcut based on two angle pairs is called AA similarity.

questions.question: In $\triangle ABC$, points $D$ and $E$ lie on $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$, and $\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}$. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: The parallel segment creates matching corresponding angles, so the smaller triangle is similar to the larger triangle in the order $A \leftrightarrow A$, $D \leftrightarrow B$, and $E \leftrightarrow C$.

questions.question: If $\triangle PQR \sim \triangle XYZ$, then vertex $Q$ corresponds to vertex ______.
questions.explanation: Corresponding vertices appear in the same position in the similarity statement: $P \leftrightarrow X$, $Q \leftrightarrow Y$, and $R \leftrightarrow Z$.

questions.question: A diagram gives $\angle M \cong \angle R$ and $\angle N \cong \angle S$. Explain why $\triangle MNP \sim \triangle RST$.
questions.correctAnswer: The triangles are similar by AA similarity because two pairs of corresponding angles are congruent: $M \leftrightarrow R$ and $N \leftrightarrow S$.
questions.explanation: The two angle pairs satisfy the AA similarity criterion, and the order $MNP$ with $RST$ preserves the stated correspondence.

questions.question: A student says $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$ because $\angle A \cong \angle D$. What is missing from the student's justification?
questions.correctAnswer: The student needs a second pair of corresponding congruent angles. One angle pair is not enough for AA similarity.
questions.explanation: AA similarity requires two angle matches. The student has only identified one, so the proof is incomplete.
